keyVerseText: And this man went up out of his city yearly to worship and to sacrifice unto the LORD of hosts in Shiloh. And the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, the priests of the LORD, were there. yearly: Heb. from year to year
rootMeaning: The name עֵלִי (ʻÊlîy) derives from the Hebrew root עָלָה (ʻâlâh), which carries the sense of ascending, rising up, or going upward. This root evokes imagery of elevation, loftiness, and exaltation, suggesting that the name Eli literally means 'ascension' or 'my God is exalted.' This etymological insight enriches the understanding of the name beyond a mere label, highlighting a spiritual dimension of rising toward God or being lifted in status or honor.
usageInScripture: The word עֵלִי appears 33 times in Scripture, predominantly as a proper name referring to the Israelite high priest Eli, who served as judge when Samuel began his ministry. The translations vary slightly but consistently identify Eli either by name or in relation to him (e.g., 'of Eli,' 'unto Eli,' 'Now Eli'), emphasizing his central role in the narrative. This consistent use underscores Eli's importance as a priestly figure and spiritual leader in Israel's history.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding Eli's name as 'ascension' or 'exalted' invites reflection on the nature of priestly ministry and God's exaltation in the Old Testament. Eli, as a high priest descended from Aaron, represents the human role in mediating between God and His people, a role ultimately fulfilled in Christ, the true High Priest who ascends and intercedes eternally. The concept of rising or being lifted up also points forward to the redemptive work of Jesus, who elevates believers to new spiritual heights. Thus, Eli's name is a reminder of God's holiness and the call to ascend spiritually in faith and obedience.
keyVerseReflection: 1 Samuel 1:3 describes a man who 'went up out of his city yearly to worship and to sacrifice unto the LORD of hosts in Shiloh,' where Eli and his sons served as priests. The word עֵלִי here identifies the high priestly figure who oversees the worship at Shiloh, anchoring the narrative in a historical and spiritual context. The name's meaning of 'ascension' resonates with the act of going up to worship, symbolizing the believer's journey toward God and the divine presence Eli represented in Israel's worship life.
